input:
# Axocoatl one-app presenter configuration.
#
# This config deliberately uses one already-installed local model. The variety
# in the Attempts comparison comes from different agent instructions, without
# paying the model-load penalty during a live presentation.

agents:
  - id: coder
    name: "Minimal Coder"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      You are a concise senior JavaScript engineer. Inspect the repository,
      make the smallest correct production change, use repository tools, run
      the configured checks, and report Root cause / Change / Proof. Do not
      alter tests to make a failure disappear. /no_think
    # `tools` is exact in a native Session: an Agent is offered only what it
    # lists. The Workspace knowledge scenario asks this Agent, the first a new
    # Session selects, to use workspace_knowledge.
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, edit_file, bash, workspace_knowledge]
    depends_on: []
    # A native Session needs an explicit output maximum; its Warn budget below
    # does not set one. Team and budget starts from this value.
    sampling: { max_tokens: 4096 }
    memory:
      core:
        blocks:
          - label: team
            limit: 1000
            shared: true
            description: "Durable facts intentionally shared by the demo team."
    token_budget: { per_execution: 6000, per_call: 3000, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: defender
    name: "Invariant Defender"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      You are a defensive JavaScript engineer. Treat tests as a contract, look
      for boundary and invariant failures, keep the patch focused, run the
      configured checks, and report Root cause / Change / Proof. Do not commit.
      /no_think
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, edit_file, bash]
    depends_on: []
    sampling: { max_tokens: 4096 }
    memory:
      core:
        blocks:
          - label: team
            limit: 1000
            shared: true
            description: "Durable facts intentionally shared by the demo team."
    token_budget: { per_execution: 6000, per_call: 3000, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: planner
    name: "Acceptance Planner"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      Turn a coding task into concise acceptance criteria, constraints, and a
      verification plan. Preserve the user's scope. /no_think
    depends_on: []
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 2000 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 4000, per_call: 2500, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: judge
    name: "Evidence Judge"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      Rank candidate changes only from repository checks, diff quality, and
      route evidence. Prefer the smallest complete change and state tradeoffs.
      /no_think
    depends_on: []
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 2000 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 4000, per_call: 2500, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: architect
    name: "Systems Architect"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      Return a concise technical design of at most 250 words. State the
      invariant, mutation sequence, concurrency rule, failure handling, and
      acceptance criteria relevant to the request. Follow only the architect
      role. Do not call tools. The words SHIP, BLOCK, and BLOCKING are reviewer
      verdict language: do not use them anywhere in your output, including the
      last line. End with acceptance criteria. /no_think
    depends_on: []
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 700 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 5000, per_call: 5000, overflow_policy: abort }

  - id: reviewer
    name: "Critical Reviewer"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      Review only the supplied direct handoffs for correctness, security,
      performance, and operability. BLOCKING means the design cannot safely
      ship as stated. Do not call tools. Give a final review of at most 200
      words: use BLOCKING only for unresolved blockers and end with a
      standalone BLOCK if any remain, otherwise SHIP.
      Never combine unresolved BLOCKING with SHIP. /no_think
    depends_on: [architect]
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 2000 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 8000, per_call: 5000, overflow_policy: abort }

  - id: investigator
    name: "Incident Investigator"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      You are the first responder in a production incident handoff. Inspect the
      production sample, lib/correlate.js, tests, and runbook. Do not edit files
      and do not use memory tools. Use no more than five repository tool calls.
      Then stop and report Evidence / Root cause / Constraints / Handoff for the
      implementer. /no_think
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob]
    depends_on: []
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 800 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 9000, per_call: 3000, overflow_policy: abort }

  - id: implementer
    name: "Incident Implementer"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      You receive an investigator's evidence before the user's request. Do not

# Axocoatl one-app presenter configuration.
#
# This config deliberately uses one already-installed local model. The variety
# in the Attempts comparison comes from different agent instructions, without
# paying the model-load penalty during a live presentation.

agents:
  - id: coder
    name: "Minimal Coder"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      You are a concise senior JavaScript engineer. Inspect the repository,
      make the smallest correct production change, use repository tools, run
      the configured checks, and report Root cause / Change / Proof. Do not
      alter tests to make a failure disappear. /no_think
    # `tools` is exact in a native Session: an Agent is offered only what it
    # lists. The Workspace knowledge scenario asks this Agent, the first a new
    # Session selects, to use workspace_knowledge.
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, edit_file, bash, workspace_knowledge]
    depends_on: []
    # A native Session needs an explicit output maximum; its Warn budget below
    # does not set one. Team and budget starts from this value.
    sampling: { max_tokens: 4096 }
    memory:
      core:
        blocks:
          - label: team
            limit: 1000
            shared: true
            description: "Durable facts intentionally shared by the demo team."
    token_budget: { per_execution: 6000, per_call: 3000, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: defender
    name: "Invariant Defender"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      You are a defensive JavaScript engineer. Treat tests as a contract, look
      for boundary and invariant failures, keep the patch focused, run the
      configured checks, and report Root cause / Change / Proof. Do not commit.
      /no_think
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, edit_file, bash]
    depends_on: []
    sampling: { max_tokens: 4096 }
    memory:
      core:
        blocks:
          - label: team
            limit: 1000
            shared: true
            description: "Durable facts intentionally shared by the demo team."
    token_budget: { per_execution: 6000, per_call: 3000, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: planner
    name: "Acceptance Planner"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      Turn a coding task into concise acceptance criteria, constraints, and a
      verification plan. Preserve the user's scope. /no_think
    depends_on: []
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 2000 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 4000, per_call: 2500, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: judge
    name: "Evidence Judge"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      Rank candidate changes only from repository checks, diff quality, and
      route evidence. Prefer the smallest complete change and state tradeoffs.
      /no_think
    depends_on: []
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 2000 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 4000, per_call: 2500, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: architect
    name: "Systems Architect"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      Return a concise technical design of at most 250 words. State the
      invariant, mutation sequence, concurrency rule, failure handling, and
      acceptance criteria relevant to the request. Follow only the architect
      role. Do not call tools. The words SHIP, BLOCK, and BLOCKING are reviewer
      verdict language: do not use them anywhere in your output, including the
      last line. End with acceptance criteria. /no_think
    depends_on: []
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 700 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 5000, per_call: 5000, overflow_policy: abort }

  - id: reviewer
    name: "Critical Reviewer"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      Review only the supplied direct handoffs for correctness, security,
      performance, and operability. BLOCKING means the design cannot safely
      ship as stated. Do not call tools. Give a final review of at most 200
      words: use BLOCKING only for unresolved blockers and end with a
      standalone BLOCK if any remain, otherwise SHIP.
      Never combine unresolved BLOCKING with SHIP. /no_think
    depends_on: [architect]
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 2000 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 8000, per_call: 5000, overflow_policy: abort }

  - id: investigator
    name: "Incident Investigator"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      You are the first responder in a production incident handoff. Inspect the
      production sample, lib/correlate.js, tests, and runbook. Do not edit files
      and do not use memory tools. Use no more than five repository tool calls.
      Then stop and report Evidence / Root cause / Constraints / Handoff for the
      implementer. /no_think
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob]
    depends_on: []
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 800 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 9000, per_call: 3000, overflow_policy: abort }

  - id: implementer
    name: "Incident Implementer"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      You receive an investigator's evidence before the user's request. Do not
      use memory tools. Read only the relevant runbook, implementation, and
      tests; apply the smallest production correction once; run npm run check
      once. If it passes, do not edit or search again: immediately report the
      exact Change / Proof / Tradeoff. Do not commit. /no_think
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, edit_file, bash]
    depends_on: [investigator]
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 800 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 10000, per_call: 3000, overflow_policy: abort }

  - id: verifier
    name: "Release Verifier"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      You receive the investigator and implementer handoffs. Inspect the actual
      diff and run npm run check exactly once. This is a read-only verification:
      never edit files and never use memory tools. Return SHIP or BLOCK with the
      exact diff meaning, check result, and one Remaining risk, then stop.
      /no_think
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, bash]
    depends_on: [implementer]
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 700 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 9000, per_call: 3000, overflow_policy: abort }

  - id: weather
    name: "Weather MCP Agent"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    system_prompt: |
      For every weather request, call mcp__weather__get_weather with the city
      before answering. Never invent conditions and never answer from memory.
      Return the tool result in one concise sentence. /no_think
    tools: [mcp__weather__get_weather]
    depends_on: []
    token_budget: { per_execution: 2500, per_call: 1500, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: incident-response

input:
# Axocoatl presenter configuration for the Lead-with-helpers film.
#
# This is the default team `axocoatl init` writes: Lead owns the change and is
# the only Agent that edits files; Scout and Reviewer are read-only Workers
# (`writes: []`) that Lead can delegate to once Team and budget approves their
# limits. It is a separate file because Worker templates make Team and budget
# offer helpers to every new single-Agent Session; the other scenarios keep
# axocoatl.demo.yaml. Start it with:
#
#   AXOCOATL_DEMO_CONFIG=axocoatl.team.yaml ./demo/one-app/start.sh

agents:
  - id: lead
    name: "Lead"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    role: autonomous
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, edit_file, bash]
    system_prompt: |
      You own this change. 1. Look first: find the relevant files and tests
      for code you do not know. If you have helpers, ask scout to find them.
      2. Make the change. 3. Run the check command from the project
      instructions (AXOCOATL.md), or the tests, and fix failures. 4. Check
      your diff against the task. If you have helpers, ask reviewer to review
      it. Fix each defect found. Then summarize what you changed. /no_think
    sampling: { max_tokens: 4096 }

  - id: scout
    name: "Scout"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    role: worker
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, bash]
    writes: []
    system_prompt: |
      Answer the lead's question with file paths, line numbers and short
      evidence. Change nothing. /no_think
    sampling: { max_tokens: 4096 }

  - id: reviewer
    name: "Reviewer"
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen3:8b
    role: worker
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, bash]
    writes: []
    system_prompt: |
      Review the described change. Check it against the task and against every
      contract and edge case the docs, comments and tests describe, one by one.
      Report each defect with file:line, or say you found none. Change nothing.
      /no_think
    sampling: { max_tokens: 4096 }

# start.sh exports AXOCOATL_DEMO_OLLAMA_PORT (default 11434) after checking
# that this local Ollama service reports cloud models disabled.
providers:
  ollama:
    base_url: "http://127.0.0.1:${AXOCOATL_DEMO_OLLAMA_PORT}"

server:
  host: "127.0.0.1"
  port: 18080

# Axocoatl — Anthropic setup
agents:
  # Default team. Lead owns the change; Scout and Reviewer are read-only
  # helpers it can delegate to once you opt in and approve their limits in
  # Team & budget. A new Session starts with Lead alone.
  - id: lead
    name: "Lead"
    provider: anthropic
    model: "claude-sonnet-4-6"
    role: autonomous
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, edit_file, bash]
    system_prompt: "You own this change. 1. Look first: find the relevant files and tests for code you do not know. If you have helpers, ask scout to find them. 2. Make the change. 3. Run the check command from the project instructions (AXOCOATL.md), or the tests, and fix failures. 4. Check your diff against the task. If you have helpers, ask reviewer to review it. Fix each defect found. Then summarize what you changed."

  - id: scout
    name: "Scout"
    provider: anthropic
    model: "claude-sonnet-4-6"
    role: worker
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, bash]
    writes: []
    system_prompt: "Answer the lead's question with file paths, line numbers and short evidence. Change nothing."

  - id: reviewer
    name: "Reviewer"
    provider: anthropic
    model: "claude-sonnet-4-6"
    role: worker
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, bash]
    writes: []
    system_prompt: "Review the described change. Check it against the task and against every contract and edge case the docs, comments and tests describe, one by one. Report each defect with file:line, or say you found none. Change nothing."

  # Plain chat for `axocoatl chat`; not part of the default team.
  - id: assistant
    name: "Assistant"
    provider: anthropic
    model: "claude-sonnet-4-6"
    system_prompt: "You are a helpful assistant."
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob]
    token_budget:
      per_execution: 20000
      per_call: 8192
      overflow_policy: summarize

providers:
  anthropic:
    api_key: "sk-test"

server:
  port: 8080
  host: "127.0.0.1"

# Axocoatl — MCP example config
#
# Two independent things live here, matching the two halves of the README:
#
#   • `mcp_servers:` — external MCP servers Axocoatl connects to AS A CLIENT.
#     The daemon dials each one at startup, runs the MCP handshake, and folds
#     their tools into the agent tool set under qualified `mcp__<server>__<tool>`
#     names (the same discovery this example's Part 1 does in-process).
#
#   • `agents:` — your own agents. `axocoatl mcp serve -c this-file.yaml`
#     exposes each one to OTHER MCP clients as an `agent_<id>` tool. That's the
#     SERVER path (README "Path B").
#
# Copy to `axocoatl.yaml` (or pass with `-c`) to use it.

# ─── MCP servers Axocoatl consumes (client path) ────────────────────────────
mcp_servers:
  # stdio transport: Axocoatl spawns the command as a child process and speaks
  # JSON-RPC over its stdin/stdout. This is how most local MCP servers ship
  # (filesystem, git, sqlite, the official reference servers via `npx`). `env`
  # is layered onto the child's environment — most servers read their API key
  # or token from there and exit before the handshake if it's missing.
  - name: filesystem
    transport: stdio
    command: npx
    args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/tmp"]
    env: {}

  # The example in this folder uses exactly this stdio shape, except `command`
  # is the example binary itself launched with `--mcp-server`. To point a real
  # daemon at it instead, you'd write:
  #
  #   - name: weather
  #     transport: stdio
  #     command: /absolute/path/to/mcp-bridge
  #     args: ["--mcp-server"]

  # streamable_http transport: a remote MCP server reached over HTTP. Use this
  # for hosted servers. `headers` is where bearer tokens / API keys go. (SSE was
  # removed upstream in rmcp 0.11; streamable HTTP is the remote transport now.)
  - name: remote-tools
    transport: streamable_http
    url: https://mcp.example.com/mcp
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer "

# ─── Your agents (exposed when you run `axocoatl mcp serve`) ─────────────────
# `axocoatl mcp serve` exposes each of these as an `agent_<id>` MCP tool. A host
# (Claude Desktop, another Axocoatl, any MCP client) lists `agent_weather` and
# calls it with `{ "input": "What's the weather in Tokyo?" }`.
agents:
  - id: weather
    name: "Weather Agent"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You answer weather questions. Use the available tools to look up conditions, then reply in one sentence."
    depends_on: []
    # `tools` declares the capabilities this agent advertises — used for
    # capability-based task routing (a Coordinator assigns work only to an agent
    # that has the required tools). Names use the qualified
    # `mcp__<server>__<tool>` form. Per-call authorization of MCP tools is a
    # separate, runtime concern handled by the human-in-the-loop approval gate
    # and the persisted permission store (see crates/axocoatl-mcp).
    tools:
      - mcp__filesystem__read_file
    token_budget: { per_execution: 2000, per_call: 1000, overflow_policy: warn }

# Axocoatl — Multi-provider routing (LIVE mode)
#
# This is the live-mode companion to the `multi-provider` example. The Rust
# binary (`cargo run -p multi-provider`) runs the same shape with mock
# providers and zero API keys. This file runs it against a REAL local Ollama
# model and a REAL frontier model, so you can see the cost contrast on your own
# bill instead of illustrative mock prices.
#
# ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
# │  COST WARNING                                                          │
# │  The `synthesizer` agent calls a HOSTED frontier model (Anthropic      │
# │  Claude Sonnet) on every run. That step costs real money — roughly     │
# │  $3 / 1M input tokens + $15 / 1M output tokens at current list price.  │
# │  The `triage` and `drafter` agents run locally via Ollama and are free │
# │  to run. Set a `token_budget` (below) on the frontier agent so a       │
# │  runaway loop can't ring up a surprise bill.                           │
# └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
#
# Preflight (see the README for the full walkthrough):
#   ollama serve &
#   ollama pull llama3.2:3b
#   export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...        # never commit this
#   axocoatl doctor --config axocoatl.multi-provider.yaml   # verifies both
#   axocoatl dev    --config axocoatl.multi-provider.yaml
#
# `axocoatl doctor` checks that Ollama is reachable, that each Ollama agent's
# model is pulled, and that the frontier provider has a non-empty API key.

# ─── Agents ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each agent names its own `provider:` — that is the per-agent routing. The
# provider name must match a key under `providers:` at the bottom of the file.
agents:
  # triage + drafter: cheap, high-volume steps → local model. Free to run.
  - id: triage
    name: "Triage"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2:3b
    system_prompt: "You are a triage agent. Classify the request and name the sub-questions a researcher should answer. Be terse."
    depends_on: []
    token_budget: { per_execution: 2000, per_call: 1000, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: drafter
    name: "Drafter"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2:3b
    system_prompt: "You are a drafter. Using the triage notes, write a quick, rough first-pass answer. Don't polish it — the synthesizer will."
    depends_on: [triage]
    token_budget: { per_execution: 3000, per_call: 1500, overflow_policy: warn }

  # synthesizer: the one expensive step → hosted frontier model. `overflow_policy:
  # abort` is deliberate here — a cost cap on the paid tier should be ENFORCED,
  # not merely logged, so a loop can't run up the bill.
  - id: synthesizer
    name: "Synthesizer"
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-sonnet-4-6
    system_prompt: "You are a senior synthesizer. Read the triage classification AND the rough draft, then write the final, polished answer with a crisp contrast paragraph."
    depends_on: [triage, drafter]
    token_budget: { per_execution: 6000, per_call: 4000, overflow_policy: abort }

# ─── Workflow ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A Lattice session runs these session-scoped agents in dependency order:
# triage, then drafter, then synthesizer once both prior outputs are
# available. The companion mock binary runs the same order with mock providers.
workflows:
  - id: route-and-synthesize
    name: "Route and synthesize"
    description: "Cheap local triage + draft, then one frontier synthesis pass."
    agents: [triage, drafter, synthesizer]
    entry_point: triage

# ─── Providers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `ollama` runs locally — no key, just a reachable base_url. `anthropic` reads
# its key from the environment via ${ENV_VAR} interpolation, so the secret is
# NEVER committed to this file. An unset variable interpolates to an empty
# string, which `axocoatl doctor` flags before you spend anything.
providers:
  ollama:
    base_url: "http://localhost:11434"
  anthropic:
    api_key: "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}"
    # To use OpenAI instead, swap the synthesizer's `provider:` to `openai`,
    # its `model:` to e.g. `gpt-4o`, and uncomment:
    # openai:
    #   api_key: "${OPENAI_API_KEY}"

# ─── Server ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
server:
  port: 8080
  host: "127.0.0.1"

# Axocoatl — minimal starter config
#
# The default team (a lead and two read-only helpers), one two-node legacy
# workflow seed and one Skill. Designed for a first run with Ollama + llama3.2
# (no hosted-provider API key needed).
#
# To use:
#   cp axocoatl.example.yaml axocoatl.yaml
#   ollama serve &
#   ollama pull llama3.2
#   axocoatl dev
#
# Then open the sign-in link `axocoatl dev` prints (or run `axocoatl url`),
# create a folder-anchored Session on Lead, and open Team & budget. The
# Session starts with Lead alone: enter its limits, Apply, and send a request
# in the Session chat. To add Scout and Reviewer as Lead's read-only helpers,
# select "Let this Agent delegate to helpers" and enter their limits too. On
# a fresh data directory, the workflow below seeds a manual Automation that is
# also available through the compatibility HTTP API.
#
# The larger demo config, including scheduled seeds and MCP servers, lives in
# axocoatl.yaml. Use that once you're past first contact.

# ─── Agents ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
agents:
  # Default team. Lead owns the change and is the only one that edits files.
  # Scout and Reviewer are Workers with `writes: []`: read-only helpers Lead
  # can delegate to once you select "Let this Agent delegate to helpers" in
  # Team & budget and approve their limits; until then Lead works alone. To
  # change the team, edit these entries (or add Workers with `writes: []`).
  - id: lead
    name: "Lead"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    role: autonomous
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, edit_file, bash]
    system_prompt: "You own this change. 1. Look first: find the relevant files and tests for code you do not know. If you have helpers, ask scout to find them. 2. Make the change. 3. Run the check command from the project instructions (AXOCOATL.md), or the tests, and fix failures. 4. Check your diff against the task. If you have helpers, ask reviewer to review it. Fix each defect found. Then summarize what you changed."
    sampling: { max_tokens: 4096 }

  - id: scout
    name: "Scout"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    role: worker
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, bash]
    writes: []
    system_prompt: "Answer the lead's question with file paths, line numbers and short evidence. Change nothing."
    sampling: { max_tokens: 4096 }

  - id: reviewer
    name: "Reviewer"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    role: worker
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, bash]
    writes: []
    system_prompt: "Review the described change. Check it against the task and against every contract and edge case the docs, comments and tests describe, one by one. Report each defect with file:line, or say you found none. Change nothing."
    sampling: { max_tokens: 4096 }

  # A two-Agent Automation example, separate from the default team.
  - id: researcher
    name: "Researcher"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You research a question and return 3 bullet-pointed facts."
    depends_on: []
    token_budget: { per_execution: 2000, per_call: 1000, overflow_policy: warn }
    # Per-agent memory tuning (all optional). The agent also gets the
    # recall_search / recall_timeframe + core_memory_* tools automatically.
    # memory:
    #   recall:                 # passive Tier-4 injection + the recall tools
    #     passive_inject: true  # inject top-k semantic hits each turn (false = pull-only)
    #     top_k: 5
    #     min_score: 0.15
    #   core:                   # Tier-3 editable blocks (default: persona/human/project)
    #     blocks:
    #       - { label: persona, limit: 2000 }
    #       - { label: human, limit: 2000 }
    #       - { label: team, limit: 1000, shared: true }  # cross-agent team memory

  - id: summarizer
    name: "Summarizer"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You take research bullets and write a single 2-sentence summary."
    depends_on: [researcher]
    token_budget: { per_execution: 2000, per_call: 1000, overflow_policy: warn }

# ─── Legacy workflow seed ───────────────────────────────────────────
# On first boot this becomes a manual Automation with an explicit dependency
# edge: the executor runs researcher before summarizer.
workflows:
  - id: hello-world
    name: "Hello world"
    description: "Research → summarize. A two-node manual Automation seed."
    agents: [researcher, summarizer]
    entry_point: researcher

# ─── Skill ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Firing a Skill publishes each event in `emits` on the event feed. Add an
# OnSkill or OnEvent Automation, or a webhook, to react to it.
skills:
  - id: quick-research
    name: "Quick research"
    description: "Publish a ResearchRequested event on the event feed."
    emits: ["ResearchRequested"]

# ─── Sleep-time memory consolidation ────────────────────────────────
# Idle agents periodically promote durable facts from their semantic memory
# into their curated core-memory blocks. On by default; tune or disable here.
# consolidation:
#   enabled: true
#   idle_threshold_secs: 120   # how long an agent must be idle before a pass runs
#   interval_secs: 1800        # minimum time between passes for one agent

# ─── Session sandbox ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Local Podman with outbound access (`bridge`) is the default. For a
# repository you do not trust, use `none`, or `egress` to let Agents' commands
# reach only the registries and hosts you list. See the Sandboxes docs page.
# sandbox:
#   network: egress
#   egress:
#     allow:
#       - npm                     # registry.npmjs.org
#       - pypi                    # pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org
#       - host: api.example.com   # ports default to [443]
#     routes:                     # TLS ended on this computer; each request checked
#       - host: github.com
#         credential: github      # added by the daemon, never in a container
#         inject: {basic: {username: x-access-token}}
#         rules:
#           - {methods: [GET], path: /acme/app.git/info/refs, query: {service: git-upload-pack}}
#           - {methods: [POST], path: /acme/app.git/git-upload-pack}
#   workload:
#     mode: auto                  # hardened under egress: Agents and helpers run as
#                                 # separate non-root users; image elsewhere
# credentials:
#   github: {env: GITHUB_TOKEN}   # read by the daemon when a request needs it

# ─── Web research (optional) ────────────────────────────────────────
# Agents whose `tools` list web_search or web_fetch can search the web
# through a SearXNG container Axocoatl runs with Podman, and read public
# pages. Both run on this computer, not in the Session container, and each
# call is kept in the Session's network record. Search queries go to public
# search engines. See the docs: Configure > Web research.
# web_search:
#   provider: searxng
# web_fetch: {}

# ─── Browser tools ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `browser` and `browser_check` run a headless Chromium in a container of its
# own that reaches this Session's exposed ports and nothing else, unless you
# declare hosts. Build the image once with `axocoatl browser install`, then
# list the tools in an Agent's `tools`.
# browser:
#   allow: []                 # declared hosts, reached through Axocoatl's egress proxy
#   snapshot_max_bytes: 16384
#   timeout_secs: 120
#   max_parallel: 2

    sampling: { max_tokens: 4096 }

  # ── Research team ────────────────────────────────────────
  - id: researcher
    name: "Researcher"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You are a research assistant. Provide detailed, factual answers with supporting context."
    depends_on: []
    token_budget: { per_execution: 8000, per_call: 4000, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: summarizer
    name: "Summarizer"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You are a summarizer. Condense input into 2-3 sentences."
    depends_on: [researcher]
    token_budget: { per_execution: 3000, per_call: 1500, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: analyst
    name: "Data Analyst"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You are a data analyst. Extract insights from numeric or textual data."
    depends_on: []
    token_budget: { per_execution: 5000, per_call: 2500, overflow_policy: warn }

  # ── Ops team ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  - id: ops
    name: "Ops Engineer"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You are a site reliability engineer. Produce deployment plans and incident responses."
    depends_on: []
    token_budget: { per_execution: 4000, per_call: 2000, overflow_policy: warn }

  # ── Customer-facing team ─────────────────────────────────
  - id: support
    name: "Support Agent"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You are a friendly customer support agent. Triage incoming issues and propose next steps."
    depends_on: []
    token_budget: { per_execution: 4000, per_call: 2000, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: secretary
    name: "Secretary"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You are an executive secretary. Prepare daily briefings, summarize meetings, draft messages."
    depends_on: []
    token_budget: { per_execution: 4000, per_call: 2000, overflow_policy: warn }

# ───────────── LEGACY AUTOMATION SEED INPUT ───────────────────
# These workflow, schedule, and proactive records seed AutomationStore only
# when its canonical automations file does not exist. After first boot, edit
# Automations in Settings; this YAML is no longer a second live registry.

workflows:
  - id: research-and-summarize
    name: "Research & Summarize"
    agents: [researcher, summarizer]
    entry_point: researcher

  - id: release-checklist
    name: "Release Readiness"
    agents: [ops]
    entry_point: ops

  - id: daily-briefing
    name: "Daily Briefing"
    agents: [secretary]
    entry_point: secretary

# ─────────────────────────── INTERVALS ─────────────────────────
# Interval-triggered Automations. Exact wall-clock/cron scheduling is not part
# of the current trigger contract.

schedules:
  - id: morning-briefing
    name: "Hourly Team Pulse"
    workflow: daily-briefing
    every: "1h"
    input: "Produce a 5-bullet update on changes, blockers, and next actions since the last run."
    enabled: true

  - id: release-pulse
    name: "Release Pulse Check"
    workflow: release-checklist
    every: "6h"
    input: "Run the standard release readiness checks for the current build."
    enabled: false

  - id: research-sync
    name: "Weekly Research Sync"
    workflow: research-and-summarize
    every: "7d"
    input: "Summarize the latest developments in self-coordinating multi-agent AI systems."
    enabled: true

# ─────────────────────────── SKILLS ───────────────────────────
# A Skill is a named set of events. Firing it (Settings → Skills,
# `POST /api/skills/{id}/fire`, or an Agent calling its `skill_<id>` tool in a
# Session that enables it) publishes each event in `emits` on the event feed.
# OnSkill and OnEvent Automations and outbound webhooks react to those events;
# the Skill itself runs nothing. Skills are the only source of these events.

skills:
  - id: review-requested
    name: "Review requested"
    description: "Announce that the current change is ready for review."
    emits: ["ReviewRequested"]

  - id: incident-resolved
    name: "Incident resolved"
    description: "Announce that the open incident is resolved."
    emits: ["IncidentResolved"]

  - id: release-ready
    name: "Release ready"
    description: "Announce that a release candidate is ready for notes and checks."
    emits: ["ReleaseReady"]

# ─────────────────────────── PROVIDERS / SERVER ───────────────

providers:
  ollama:
    base_url: "http://localhost:11434"

server:
  port: 8080
  # Loopback by default. With no auth below, the API requires the per-daemon
  # token in <data>/local-api-token; `axocoatl url` prints the sign-in link.
  host: "127.0.0.1"
  # To expose Axocoatl on the network you MUST configure auth, or the server
  # refuses to start. Tokens support ${ENV_VAR} interpolation.
  # host: "0.0.0.0"
  # auth:
  #   api_keys: ["${AXOCOATL_API_KEY}"]
  #   bearer_tokens: ["${AXOCOATL_BEARER}"]
  #   # allow_unauthenticated: true   # only if an upstream proxy enforces auth
  # cors_origins: ["https://your-dashboard.example.com"]

# ─────────────────────────── SESSION SANDBOX ───────────────────
# Trust + isolation policy for the per-session podman containers. Defaults are
# secure: opening a repository will NOT run its setup scripts or pull an
# attacker-chosen image. Loosen these only for repositories you trust.
sandbox:
  # Run a repo's devcontainer postCreateCommand automatically on session open.
  # Off by default — otherwise a hostile repo gets code execution on open.
  allow_post_create_command: false
  # Honor a repo/UI base image other than the trusted default (alpine).
  allow_untrusted_images: false
  # "bridge" (default: outbound + published dev ports) or "none" (no network —
  # blocks exfiltration for untrusted code, but also installs and dev servers).
  network: "bridge"
  # Refuse to start a session if memory/CPU/pid caps can't be applied, instead
  # of silently running uncapped. Leave false on hosts without cgroup delegation
  # (e.g. rootless podman on WSL2).
  require_resource_limits: false

# ───────────────────── LEGACY PROACTIVE SEEDS ──────────────────
# These become Automations on first boot. The Always-On Service
# (`axocoatl service install`) keeps the daemon alive so enabled interval and
# event triggers can dispatch while the app is not open.

proactive:
  - id: hourly-briefing
    name: "Hourly Briefing"
    agent: secretary
    trigger:
      type: schedule
      every: 1h
    input: "Give a concise one-paragraph briefing on recent activity and anything that needs attention."
    enabled: true

  - id: postmortem-watch
    name: "Postmortem Drafter"
    agent: ops
    trigger:
      type: on_event
      event: IncidentResolved          # published when the incident-resolved Skill fires
    input: "An incident was just resolved. Draft a blameless postmortem outline: timeline, root cause, impact, mitigation, action items."
    enabled: true

# Axocoatl — project-local configuration (local Ollama)
# See: https://docs.axocoatl.ai/configure/agents/

agents:
  # Default team. Lead owns the change; Scout and Reviewer are read-only
  # helpers it can delegate to once you opt in and approve their limits in
  # Team & budget. A new Session starts with Lead alone.
  - id: lead
    name: "Lead"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    role: autonomous
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, edit_file, bash]
    system_prompt: "You own this change. 1. Look first: find the relevant files and tests for code you do not know. If you have helpers, ask scout to find them. 2. Make the change. 3. Run the check command from the project instructions (AXOCOATL.md), or the tests, and fix failures. 4. Check your diff against the task. If you have helpers, ask reviewer to review it. Fix each defect found. Then summarize what you changed."
    sampling:
      max_tokens: 4096

  - id: scout
    name: "Scout"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    role: worker
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, bash]
    writes: []
    system_prompt: "Answer the lead's question with file paths, line numbers and short evidence. Change nothing."
    sampling:
      max_tokens: 4096

  - id: reviewer
    name: "Reviewer"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    role: worker
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, bash]
    writes: []
    system_prompt: "Review the described change. Check it against the task and against every contract and edge case the docs, comments and tests describe, one by one. Report each defect with file:line, or say you found none. Change nothing."
    sampling:
      max_tokens: 4096

  # Plain chat for `axocoatl chat`; not part of the default team.
  - id: assistant
    name: "Assistant"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You are a helpful assistant."
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob]
    token_budget:
      per_execution: 16000
      per_call: 8192
      overflow_policy: warn

providers:
  ollama:
    base_url: "http://localhost:11434"
  # A hosted provider reads its key from the process environment; see
  # https://docs.axocoatl.ai/configure/providers/ and .env.example.

server:
  port: 8080
  host: "127.0.0.1"

# Built-in loadout: audit (opt-in). Owner: workstream audit.
#
# Turns in one Session, each after its own Team and budget Apply:
#   1. plan: the planner splits the scope into 2-8 areas (an AREAS JSON
#      block); an invalid plan, or a planner without an answer, gets one
#      retry, and a second attempt without a plan leaves the whole scope not
#      covered;
#   2. areas: the host lists the repository's files (git ls-files, or a walk
#      outside Git) and gives each to the first area whose paths match it,
#      else to the area sharing its directories, else to a host-made area
#      "rest"; it splits an area whose files need more reads than one worker
#      makes within its invocations into numbered sub-areas; then it runs one
#      read-only worker without a shell per area in parallel (at most 16
#      workers and 200 planned reads to a turn, more in further turns), each
#      told its files, with a fresh context and no dependencies (no checks,
#      no review);
#   3. follow-ups: a worker that left files of its area unread (judged from
#      the bytes the read_file calls its Session recorded returned, never
#      from its answer) gets another activation naming exactly those files,
#      again for as long as each one reads something new;
#   4. integrate: the integrator merges every worker's report. Integration is
#      its own turn, so the integrator has no depends_on. The host then checks
#      the findings against its listing: one at a file the repository does not
#      have is a note, a line beyond its file becomes unknown, and near
#      duplicates (same file, lines at most 2 apart, similar titles) are
#      reported once.
# Each file still unread is listed as not covered, and so is a worker without
# a result, which makes the run need attention (exit 2). Empty and binary
# files need no read; a file over 256 KiB is a note. A worker's NOT_REACHED
# list is a note.
# Findings alone do not change the exit code unless fail_on_findings is true.
#
# Measured trade-off, not an Axocoatl result: on an audit larger than one
# context, orchestrated read-only area workers had recall +11 points (99% vs
# 87%) and precision -8 points at about 3x the tokens and the same wall time,
# measured with Claude Code subagents on Claude Opus (not through Axocoatl).
# The +11 is a sensitivity analysis (the study's preregistered exclusion rule
# excluded 9 of 10 attempts), not a preregistered result.
schema: axocoatl.loadout/1
id: audit
version: 1
name: Audit
description: >-
  Plan the scope into areas, audit each area in parallel with a fresh
  read-only worker, then integrate. Use it when the scope is larger than one
  context. Measured with Claude Code subagents, not Axocoatl: about three times
  the tokens of one agent (a sensitivity analysis).
kind: audit
opt_in: true
params:
  planner_model:
    kind: model
    required: true
    description: provider:model of the planner
  worker_model:
    kind: model
    required: true
    description: provider:model of each area worker
  integrator_model:
    kind: model
    required: true
    description: provider:model of the integrator
agents:
  - id: planner
    role: planner
    model: { param: planner_model }
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob]
    writes: []
    instructions: >-
      Read enough of the repository to split the scope into areas that
      together cover it without overlap, each small enough for one context,
      and name each area's files in its paths. Change nothing. Answer with
      one AREAS JSON block only.
  - id: worker
    role: worker
    model: { param: worker_model }
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob]
    writes: []
    instructions: >-
      Audit only your area. Change nothing; you have no shell and no tool
      that writes. Read every file your instructions name with read_file.
      Report each defect with file:line, evidence and severity in a FINDINGS
      JSON block, and list any file of yours you could not examine, with why,
      in a NOT_REACHED JSON block ([] when there is none). The other areas of
      the plan are audited by other workers.
  - id: integrator
    role: integrator
    model: { param: integrator_model }
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob]
    writes: []
    instructions: >-
      The host gives you every area worker's findings in one turn after the
      areas finish. Merge them: remove duplicates, keep every distinct defect
      with its area, and answer with one FINDINGS JSON block.
audit:
  min_areas: 2
  max_areas: 8
  fail_on_findings: false
budgets:
  agent: { activations: 2, invocations: 300, tokens: 3000000, cost_usd: 8 }
  wall_clock: 120m
prompt: |
  Audit this repository: {task}
sandbox:
  network: egress
  workload: hardened

input:
# Built-in loadout: fix. Owner: workstream review-qa.
# One writer, the project's required checks, and a required review by a
# different model (up to three rounds). The reviewer numbers its findings
# F1, F2, ...; the writer answers every finding the host sends back with
# accept or reject and a reason, in an ADJUDICATIONS block, and the host
# records each answer (a finding left unanswered is "missing" and the run
# needs attention). A reviewer on the writer's model is warned about, not
# refused.
schema: axocoatl.loadout/1
id: fix
version: 1
name: Fix
description: >-
  One writer makes the change; the host runs the required checks on the exact
  final files and a reviewer on a different model must approve the result.
kind: fix
mystery: 1
params:
  writer_model:
    kind: model
    required: true
    description: provider:model of the writer
  reviewer_model:
    kind: model
    required: true
    description: provider:model of the reviewer (use a different model than the writer)
agents:
  - id: writer
    role: writer
    model: { param: writer_model }
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, edit_file, bash]
    instructions: >-
      You own this change. Find the relevant code and tests, make the change,
      run the project's check command and fix failures, then compare your diff
      with the task. When the host sends you review findings, answer every
      finding in an ADJUDICATIONS block: a line ADJUDICATIONS, then a fenced
      JSON array with one object per finding, {"id": "F1", "decision":
      "accept" or "reject", "reason": "..."}. Reject only with a concrete
      reason (the code that shows the finding is wrong). Fix each finding you
      accept, run the checks again, and give your final answer.
checks:
  - name: tests
    run: { detected: true }
    timeout: 3m
review:
  model: { param: reviewer_model }
  rounds: 3
  tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob]
  adjudicate: true
  instructions: >-
    Review the change against the task and against every contract and edge
    case the docs, comments and tests describe. Read the code the change
    touches, not only the diff. Number each finding F1, F2, ... at the start
    of its line, with file:line, what is wrong and what to change; report
    only defects, not style. Give the verdict line the host asks for,
    VERDICT: APPROVE or VERDICT: CHANGES. Change nothing.
budgets:
  agent: { activations: 4, invocations: 400, tokens: 4000000, cost_usd: 10 }
  reviewer: { activations: 3, invocations: 120, tokens: 1500000, cost_usd: 3 }
  wall_clock: 60m
prompt: |
  {task}
sandbox:
  network: egress
  workload: hardened

input:
# Built-in loadout: fix. Owner: workstream review-qa.
# One writer, the project's required checks, and a required review by a
# different model (up to three rounds). The reviewer numbers its findings
# F1, F2, ...; the writer answers every finding the host sends back with
# accept or reject and a reason, in an ADJUDICATIONS block, and the host
# records each answer (a finding left unanswered is "missing" and the run
# needs attention). A reviewer on the writer's model is warned about, not
# refused.
schema: axocoatl.loadout/1
id: fix
version: 1
name: Fix
description: >-
  One writer makes the change; the host runs the required checks on the exact
  final files and a reviewer on a different model must approve the result.
kind: fix
params:
  writer_model:
    kind: model
    required: true
    description: provider:model of the writer
  reviewer_model:
    kind: model
    required: true
    description: provider:model of the reviewer (use a different model than the writer)
agents:
  - id: writer
    role: writer
    model: { param: writer_model }
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, edit_file, bash]
    instructions: >-
      You own this change. Find the relevant code and tests, make the change,
      run the project's check command and fix failures, then compare your diff
      with the task. When the host sends you review findings, answer every
      finding in an ADJUDICATIONS block: a line ADJUDICATIONS, then a fenced
      JSON array with one object per finding, {"id": "F1", "decision":
      "accept" or "reject", "reason": "..."}. Reject only with a concrete
      reason (the code that shows the finding is wrong). Fix each finding you
      accept, run the checks again, and give your final answer.
checks:
  - name: tests
    run: { detected: true }
    timeout: 3m
review:
  model: { param: reviewer_model }
  rounds: 3
  tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob]
  adjudicate: true
  instructions: >-
    Review the change against the task and against every contract and edge
    case the docs, comments and tests describe. Read the code the change
    touches, not only the diff. Number each finding F1, F2, ... at the start
    of its line, with file:line, what is wrong and what to change; report
    only defects, not style. Give the verdict line the host asks for,
    VERDICT: APPROVE or VERDICT: CHANGES. Change nothing.
budgets:
  agent: { activations: 4, invocations: 400, tokens: 4000000, cost_usd: 10 }
  reviewer: { activations: 3, invocations: 120, tokens: 1500000, cost_usd: 3 }
  wall_clock: 60m
prompt: |
  {task}
sandbox:
  network: bridge
  workload: hardened

# Built-in loadout: qa. Owner: workstream review-qa.
# One browser explorer; no scouts, no merge, no verifier. Every finding needs
# an executable reproduction (a Playwright test under repro_dir). With a
# reference build, a finding is confirmed only when its reproduction fails on
# the build under test and passes on the reference; one that also fails on the
# reference is listed as "fails on clean build", never confirmed. Areas the
# explorer did not reach or was blocked on are listed as not covered, never a
# silent pass.
#
# repro_dir is a visible directory: browser_check reads only repository paths
# whose segments start with a letter, a digit, '_', '@' or '+', so a hidden
# directory such as .axocoatl/ could not be re-run.
schema: axocoatl.loadout/1
id: qa
version: 1
name: QA
description: >-
  One explorer drives the app in a browser and reports findings, each with an
  executable reproduction the host re-runs against the build under test and,
  when configured, a clean reference build.
kind: qa
params:
  explorer_model:
    kind: model
    required: true
    description: provider:model of the explorer (needs tool calls)
  target_url:
    kind: url
    default: http://localhost:3000
    description: the build under test, as the browser container reaches it
  reference_url:
    kind: url
    description: a clean reference build; without it findings are reproduced, not confirmed
agents:
  - id: explorer
    role: explorer
    model: { param: explorer_model }
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, browser, browser_check]
    writes: ["axocoatl-qa/**"]
    instructions: >-
      You test a running web app in a browser and report its bugs. Work area
      by area (pages, flows, forms, error states) and keep a list of the areas
      you know of. Use browser to explore. For every bug you report, write one
      Playwright test file under axocoatl-qa/, such as
      axocoatl-qa/b1-coupon-total.spec.ts, that imports test and expect from
      @playwright/test, opens pages relative to the base URL
      (page.goto('/cart')), and fails because of the bug, not because of a
      typo or a timeout. Run it with browser_check, passing the build under
      test as base_url, and report the bug only when the test fails for that
      reason. Change no other file. End your answer with two fenced JSON
      blocks. First a line FINDINGS, then a JSON array with one object per
      bug: {"id": "B1", "title": "...", "area": "...", "severity":
      "low|medium|high|critical", "expected": "...", "actual": "...",
      "repro": "axocoatl-qa/b1-....spec.ts"}, or [] when you found none. Then
      a line COVERAGE, then a JSON array with one object per area: {"area":
      "...", "status": "covered|not_reached|blocked", "reason": "..."}. List
      every area you know of, the ones you did not reach or could not test
      included, with the reason. An area you leave out counts as not covered.
qa:
  target_url: { param: target_url }
  reference_url: { param: reference_url }
  repro_dir: axocoatl-qa
  fail_on_findings: true
budgets:
  agent: { activations: 2, invocations: 600, tokens: 10000, cost_usd: 15 }
  wall_clock: 90m
prompt: |
  Explore the app at {target_url} and report its bugs. Pass {target_url} as
  base_url to browser_check.
  {task}
sandbox:
  network: egress
  workload: hardened

# Start the provider first, then launch the release binary with this config and
# an isolated AXOCOATL_DATA_DIR / AXOCOATL_SOCKET_PATH.
agents:
  - id: coder
    name: "Minimal Coder"
    provider: ollama
    model: harbor-ways-fixture
    system_prompt: |
      You are a concise senior JavaScript engineer. Inspect the repository,
      make the smallest correct production change, use repository tools, run
      the configured checks, and report Diagnosis / Decision / Evidence /
      Tradeoff. Do not alter tests to make a failure disappear. /no_think
    depends_on: []
    token_budget: { per_execution: 6000, per_call: 3000, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: defender
    name: "Invariant Defender"
    provider: ollama
    model: harbor-ways-fixture
    system_prompt: |
      You are a defensive JavaScript engineer. Treat tests as a contract, look
      for boundary and invariant failures, keep the patch focused, run the
      configured checks, and report Diagnosis / Decision / Evidence / Tradeoff.
      Do not commit. /no_think
    depends_on: []
    token_budget: { per_execution: 6000, per_call: 3000, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: planner
    name: "Acceptance Planner"
    provider: ollama
    model: harbor-ways-fixture
    system_prompt: |
      Turn a coding task into concise acceptance criteria, constraints, and a
      verification plan. Preserve the user's scope. /no_think
    depends_on: []
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 500 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 4000, per_call: 2500, overflow_policy: warn }

  - id: judge
    name: "Evidence Judge"
    provider: ollama
    model: harbor-ways-fixture
    system_prompt: |
      Rank candidate changes only from repository checks, diff quality, and
      route evidence. Prefer the smallest complete change and state tradeoffs.
      /no_think
    depends_on: []
    sampling: { temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 500 }
    token_budget: { per_execution: 4000, per_call: 2500, overflow_policy: warn }

# Legacy Automation seed — workflow, schedule, and proactive trigger shapes.
#
# This config is used two ways:
#   1. `cargo run -p proactive-agents` parses it with axocoatl_config::parse_config
#      and projects it into canonical Automation records with a mock LLM.
#   2. `axocoatl dev -c examples/proactive-agents/axocoatl.proactive.example.yaml`
#      imports it only when that daemon has no `automations.json` file, then runs the
#      canonical store-watching dispatcher (needs Ollama, or another provider).
#
# These legacy sections are first-boot migration input. After import, edit the
# records in Settings → Automations or `/api/automations`; changing/reloading this
# YAML does not create a second live trigger registry.

# ─────────────────────────── AGENTS ───────────────────────────
# Two agents — the ones the proactive entries name. Provider is ollama so the
# daemon path needs no API key (point it at a local model). The cargo demo
# ignores the provider and substitutes a mock LLM.

agents:
  - id: ops
    name: "Ops Agent"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You are an operations agent. When a build fails, diagnose the likely cause and suggest one concrete, actionable fix. Be specific and brief."

  - id: secretary
    name: "Secretary"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You are a concise operations secretary. Produce short, factual status briefings. No fluff."

# ─────────────────────────── SKILLS ───────────────────────────
# Firing a Skill (Settings → Skills, `POST /api/skills/{id}/fire`, or an Agent
# calling its `skill_<id>` tool) publishes each event in its `emits` list on the
# event feed. A Skill's declared event is the only kind of event the daemon
# publishes, so it is what an on_event trigger can watch. The cargo demo fires
# these same Skills on its own feed.

skills:
  - id: build-failed
    name: "Build failed"
    description: "Report a failing CI build to the ops agent."
    emits: ["BuildFailed"]

  - id: deploy-finished
    name: "Deploy finished"
    description: "Announce that a deploy finished."
    emits: ["DeployFinished"]

# ─────────────────────────── WORKFLOW + SCHEDULE ──────────────
# The seed conversion turns this into `sched:briefing-run`, a Schedule
# Automation containing the referenced workflow's graph.

workflows:
  - id: daily-briefing
    name: "Daily Briefing"
    agents: [secretary]
    entry_point: secretary

schedules:
  - id: briefing-run
    name: "Briefing Run"
    workflow: daily-briefing          # fires the whole workflow above
    every: "30s"                       # 30s so local testing doesn't wait
    input: "Produce a 3-bullet briefing on recent activity."
    enabled: true

# ─────────────────────────── PROACTIVE AGENTS ─────────────────
# The seed conversion turns each entry into a `pro:<id>` Automation with one
# Agent node and a Schedule or OnEvent trigger. They join the same canonical
# store and runtime as every other Automation.

proactive:
  # (a) schedule trigger — fires one agent on a fixed interval.
  - id: hourly-briefing
    name: "Hourly Briefing"
    agent: secretary
    trigger:
      type: schedule
      every: 30s                       # 30s for local testing (would be 1h in prod)
    input: "Give a concise one-paragraph briefing on recent activity and anything that needs attention."
    enabled: true

  # (b) on_event trigger — fires one agent whenever a named event is published
  #     on the event feed. This is the entry the cargo demo drives: firing the
  #     build-failed Skill publishes BuildFailed and activates the ops agent.
  - id: failure-watch
    name: "Failure Watcher"
    agent: ops
    trigger:
      type: on_event
      event: BuildFailed               # published when the build-failed Skill fires
    input: "CI reported a failing build. Diagnose the likely cause and suggest a concrete fix."
    enabled: true

# ─────────────────────────── PROVIDERS ────────────────────────
providers:
  ollama:
    base_url: "http://localhost:11434"

# e2b-backend — run tool execution in a remote E2B microVM (opt-in isolation)
#
# The agent's file / shell / git tools run inside an E2B Cloud microVM instead of
# a local Podman container. E2B Cloud is the remote backend validated for Axocoatl
# 1.0; third-party E2B API implementations are outside the 1.0 support claim. The
# LLM still runs wherever the daemon does (here, local Ollama); only tool execution
# goes remote.
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - E2B_API_KEY in your environment
#   - For a private git-repo session: GITHUB_TOKEN with clone/push rights
#   - ollama serve && ollama pull llama3.2   (or swap in any provider)
# Run:
#   export E2B_API_KEY=e2b_...   GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_...
#   axocoatl validate examples/configs/e2b-backend.yaml
#   axocoatl dev -c examples/configs/e2b-backend.yaml
# Expected:
#   the session's tools (read/write/bash/git) execute inside the microVM; a
#   git-repo session clones the repo into the VM. Changes remain ordinary working-
#   tree state until you deliberately review, commit, and push with repository tools.
#   This backend and its template apply to every Session in this daemon. A
#   per-Session or devcontainer OCI image is rejected rather than substituted.
#   The template must already contain sh, git, and Axocoatl's required POSIX
#   repository commands; E2B readiness verifies them but does not apt/apk
#   provision the remote template.
#   Local-first stays the default — remove this `sandbox:` block (or set
#   `backend: podman`) to run everything on-box again.

# ─── Isolation backend ──────────────────────────────────────────────
sandbox:
  # podman (local container, default) | e2b (remote E2B Cloud microVM)
  backend: e2b
  e2b:
    api_url: "https://api.e2b.dev"
    api_key: "${E2B_API_KEY}"       # sourced from the environment, never committed
    template: "base"                # daemon-global E2B template id
    # Only for a private git-repo session; public repos clone without it. Read by
    # an in-VM credential helper at fill-time — never written into the repo config.
    git_token: "${GITHUB_TOKEN}"

# ─── Agents ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
agents:
  - id: assistant
    name: "Remote Assistant"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You are a coding assistant. Your file and shell tools run inside a remote microVM — use them normally."
    tools: [read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, write_file, edit_file, bash]
    depends_on: []

providers:
  ollama:
    base_url: "http://localhost:11434"

# event-webhooks — opt-in signed delivery of Skill events to your endpoint
#
# Prerequisites: ollama serve && ollama pull llama3.2
#                export WEBHOOK_SECRET=any-value   # enables HMAC-SHA256 signing
# Run:           axocoatl validate examples/configs/event-webhooks.yaml
#                axocoatl dev -c examples/configs/event-webhooks.yaml
# Expected:      validates; `axocoatl doctor` lists the configured webhook host.
#                Firing the Deploy finished Skill (Settings → Skills, or
#                POST /api/skills/deploy-finished/fire) publishes DeployFinished
#                and sends one signed JSON POST to the URL. In a Session that
#                enables the Skill, the Agent can fire it as its
#                `skill_deploy-finished` tool. Remove the `webhooks:` section and
#                the webhook dispatcher sends no requests; providers, model
#                downloads, MCP, and sandbox tools are separate egress paths.

agents:
  - id: deployer
    name: "Deployer"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You prepare and verify deploys. When a deploy is verified, fire the deploy-finished Skill."
    depends_on: []

# Firing a Skill publishes each event in `emits` on the event feed. Skills are
# the only source of events, so webhook filters name Skill events.
skills:
  - id: deploy-finished
    name: "Deploy finished"
    description: "Announce that a deploy finished and was verified."
    emits: ["DeployFinished"]

# Event-feed egress: the outbound counterpart to inbound A2A. Opt-in — with no
# `webhooks:` section the webhook dispatcher sends no requests.
webhooks:
  - name: deploy-alerts
    url: https://hooks.example.com/axocoatl
    # Event names to send. Empty ([]) means every event.
    events: [DeployFinished]
    # With a secret, each body is HMAC-SHA256 signed and the hex digest is sent
    # in `X-Axocoatl-Signature: sha256=…` so the receiver can verify it.
    secret: ${WEBHOOK_SECRET}
    # Optional static headers (e.g. an auth bearer for an internal endpoint).
    headers:
      X-Source: axocoatl

providers:
  ollama:
    base_url: "http://localhost:11434"

# feature-dev — five agents in a linear DAG (architect → … → docs)
#
# Prerequisites: ollama serve && ollama pull llama3.2  (no API key needed)
# Run:           axocoatl validate examples/configs/feature-dev.yaml

  - id: architect
    name: "Architect"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "Break the task into a clear, concise technical specification."
    depends_on: []

  - id: planner
    name: "Planner"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "Turn the spec into an ordered, actionable task list."
    depends_on: [architect]

    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "Write clear, friendly documentation for the reviewed feature."
    depends_on: [reviewer]

# incident-response — Skills that publish incident events, and the Automations
# that react to them
#
# Prerequisites: ollama serve && ollama pull llama3.2  (no API key needed)
# Run:           axocoatl validate examples/configs/incident-response.yaml
#                axocoatl dev -c examples/configs/incident-response.yaml
# Expected:      On first boot the two `proactive:` entries become OnEvent
#                Automations. Firing the Incident reported Skill (Settings →
#                Skills, or POST /api/skills/incident-reported/fire) publishes
#                IncidentReported and runs the triage Automation; firing
#                Incident resolved publishes IncidentResolved and runs the
#                postmortem Automation. A Skill event carries only the Skill id,
#                so each Agent works from its Automation's input.

agents:
  - id: ops
    name: "Ops Engineer"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "You are a site reliability engineer. Diagnose incidents and produce mitigation steps."
    depends_on: []

  - id: scribe
    name: "Scribe"
    provider: ollama
    model: llama3.2
    system_prompt: "Write clear, blameless incident postmortems."
    depends_on: []

skills:
  - id: incident-reported
    name: "Incident reported"
    description: "Announce that a new incident needs triage."
    emits: ["IncidentReported"]

  - id: incident-resolved
    name: "Incident resolved"
    description: "Announce that the open incident is resolved."
    emits: ["IncidentResolved"]

# First-boot seed: each entry becomes an OnEvent Automation with one Agent node.
proactive:
  - id: incident-triage
    name: "Incident Triage"
    agent: ops
    trigger:
      type: on_event
      event: IncidentReported
    input: "An incident was reported. List, in order, the first five checks the on-call engineer should run and what each one rules out."
    enabled: true

  - id: incident-postmortem
    name: "Incident Postmortem"
    agent: scribe
    trigger:
      type: on_event
      event: IncidentResolved
    input: "An incident was just resolved. Draft a blameless postmortem outline: timeline, root cause, impact, mitigation, action items."
    enabled: true

providers:
  ollama:
    base_url: "http://localhost:11434"

input:
name: CI
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, dev]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  workflow-contracts:
    name: Workflow contracts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - uses: actions/setup-go@d35c59abb061a4a6fb18e82ac0862c26744d6ab5 # v5
        with:
          go-version: '1.26.2'
          cache: false
      - name: Validate GitHub Actions semantics with pinned actionlint
        run: ./scripts/run-actionlint.sh
      - name: Verify workflow syntax, shell syntax, pinning, and shared gates
        run: ./scripts/check-workflow-contracts.rb
      - name: Exercise the workflow contract's verification-feature rules
        run: ./scripts/test-workflow-contracts.sh
      - name: Exercise film-gate release-candidate routing
        run: ./scripts/test-film-gate.sh
      - name: Exercise public release-state evaluation
        run: ./scripts/test-public-release.sh

  marketing-site:
    name: Marketing site
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - name: Install film inspection dependency
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg
      - name: Exercise film provenance and release compatibility contracts
        run: node --test demo/one-app/films/*.test.mjs
      - name: Exercise the incident recovery workflow contract
        run: ./scripts/test-recover-v1.0.1-workflow.sh
      - name: Build and verify the exact marketing payload
        run: ./scripts/verify-marketing-gate.sh portable /tmp/axocoatl-marketing
      - name: Require release provenance when the product version changes
        env:
          PR_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          PR_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          PUSH_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: |
          base="$PR_BASE_SHA"
          head="$PR_HEAD_SHA"
          if [ -z "$base" ]; then
            base="$PUSH_BASE_SHA"
            head="$GITHUB_SHA"
          fi
          if [ -z "$base" ] || [[ "$base" =~ ^0+$ ]]; then
            base="$(git rev-parse "$head^")"
          fi
          ./scripts/verify-film-gate.sh candidate "$base" "$head"

  docs-site:
    name: Docs site
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: sites/docs/package-lock.json
      - name: Build and verify the exact documentation payload
        run: ./scripts/verify-docs-gate.sh

  test:
    name: Test (Linux)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      - name: Verify the product browser gate is checked in
        run: |
          git ls-files --error-unmatch \
            axocoatl-server/browser-tests/package-lock.json \
            axocoatl-server/browser-tests/support/run-tests.mjs \
            axocoatl-server/browser-tests/tests/workbench.test.mjs >/dev/null
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: licenses/vendor-web/package-lock.json
      - uses: actions/setup-go@d35c59abb061a4a6fb18e82ac0862c26744d6ab5 # v5
        with:
          go-version: '1.26.2'
          cache: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@e797f83bcb11b83ae66e0230d6156d7c80228e7c # v6.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13.7'
          check-latest: false
      - name: Validate workflow semantics inside the required native check
        run: ./scripts/run-actionlint.sh
      - name: Verify workflow and shared-gate contracts inside the required native check
        run: ./scripts/check-workflow-contracts.rb
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4360b52568e2003a75bf9bc1d59f33a8e3fc893c # stable 2026-08-23
        with:
          toolchain: 1.88.0
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4360b52568e2003a75bf9bc1d59f33a8e3fc893c # stable 2026-08-23
        with:
          toolchain: 1.95.0
          components: clippy, rustfmt
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
      - name: Install the pinned audit tool
        run: cargo install cargo-audit --locked --version 0.22.2
      - name: Install the pinned license notice generator
        run: cargo install cargo-about --locked --version '=0.9.1' --features cli
      - name: Run the exact native release preflight
        run: ./scripts/verify-native-gate.sh

  msrv:
    name: Minimum Rust 1.88
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4360b52568e2003a75bf9bc1d59f33a8e3fc893c # stable 2026-08-23
        with:
          toolchain: 1.88.0
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          shared-key: msrv-1.88
      - name: Check the declared minimum toolchain
        run: cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features --jobs 1

  product-browser:
    name: Product browser regressions
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 25
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4360b52568e2003a75bf9bc1d59f33a8e3fc893c # stable 2026-08-23
        with:
          toolchain: 1.95.0
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          shared-key: product-browser
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: axocoatl-server/browser-tests/package-lock.json
      - name: Build and exercise the visible product surface
        env:
          AXO_BROWSER_INSTALL_WITH_DEPS: 'true'
        run: ./scripts/verify-product-browser-gate.sh

  cross-aarch64-linux:
    name: Cross-build (aarch64-linux)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4360b52568e2003a75bf9bc1d59f33a8e3fc893c # stable 2026-08-23
        with:
          toolchain: 1.95.0
          targets: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
      - name: Install cross linker
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu
      - name: Build the CLI for aarch64-linux
        run: ./scripts/verify-cross-linux-gate.sh build

      - name: Audit embedded assets and verify generated third-party notices
